newsitem.title: UK: Sears sales slowdown prompts downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Sears sales slowdown prompts downgrades.

text.p: Retail sector analysts downgraded current year profit forecasts for British retail conglomerate Sears Plc after the company revealed a first half sales slowdown in a statement to its annual meeting on Tuesday.
Two leading retail analysts cut their forecasts and one, who asked not to be identified, downgraded his recommendation on Sears' shares to a sell from a hold.

Analysts said forecasts for 1997/98 were being revised down to between 60 million and 71 million from around 75 million stg. The forecasts included a contribution from Sears' Freemans mail order business, which is due to be sold to retail-to-football pools group Littlewoods LWD.CN pending a monopolies enquiry.
Sears' shares were 0.5 pence lower at 70 pence by 1450 GMT.

Sears, owner of Selfridges department store plus shoe shops and women's fashion chains, reported its like-for-like sales rose by 2.5 percent in the 19 weeks to June 14, which marked a slowdown from the 5.3 percent rise the company achieved in the first 11 weeks of the year.
Analysts said the group's star performer Selfridges' had weakened slightly probably due to the impact of the strong pound on the tourist trade as well as disruption from remodelling inside the shop.
Like-for-like sales at Selfridges rose 6.3 percent in the 19-weeks, while same-store sales at its UK women's wear business jumped 13.5 percent, boosted by the roll-out of a new store format.

Analysts said the sales increase from women's wear was pleasing, but expressed concern about children's wear, where Sears said sales had slowed down in the last few weeks. The footwear division's sales declined 1.3 percent. Analysts are forecasting British Shoe will make a loss of 20 to 25 million stg in the current year.

In April Sears, which has failed to capitalise on Britain's retail recovery, announced radical restructuring plans, including the possible demerger of Selfridges and rationalisation of British Shoe to try and improve returns for shareholders.
